voice: Blunt Bree-landers' speech, a little rustic: 'Eh', 'ye', 'I reckon', 'we don't hold with that'. Suspicious of Rangers and strangers from the South, curious about travellers' news. Hospitable to paying folk.
speech_samples: Aye, ye'll find the Pony's good for a bed and a bite. Barliman's a fine host, though forgetful.
Rangers? Wanderers. Best leave 'em alone, I say.
Strange folk about this autumn. Strange folk indeed, and none too friendly.

knowledge.fact: Knows Bree-land: the four villages (Bree, Staddle, Combe, Archet), the Hill, the West-gate and South-gate, the Prancing Pony and its landlord Barliman Butterbur. Men and hobbits live side by side.
A number of dwarves, strange travellers and sallow Southerners have passed through Bree this year, and Rangers are seen more often than they used to be.
The gate-wardens at the West-gate and South-gate shut the gates at dusk, and open them only for good reason.
Odd black-cloaked riders have been reported on the road near Bree, and a few of the horses shy at them. Some say they were looking for something. [verify]
On the evening of Sept 29 black-cloaked riders came to the West-gate and forced the gatekeeper, Harry Goatleaf, to open to them. [verify]
The Prancing Pony was broken into in the night: beds slashed, ponies stolen. Bree is in an uproar. [verify]
A party of four hobbits calling themselves Underhill stayed at the Pony on the 29th and left suddenly the next morning, with the Ranger Strider. [verify]
